title: The Twin Coast Discovery Highway
lines: Taitokerau Northland’s twin coast experience is one of contrasts. Starting and finishing in Auckland, this is the ultimate journey for those who want to see, feel, and discover it all.
Taitokerau Northland’s twin coast experience is one of contrasts. Starting and finishing in Auckland, this is the ultimate journey for those who want to see, feel, and discover it all

Pick and choose from a huge range of activities along this 800km circular touring route. Seven days is just enough for a taster of the region, so you may like to extend your trip and stay a few extra nights to fit in everything suggested below.

Wind your way through to Ahipara, the southern end of Te Oneroa a Tōhē Ninety Mile Beach. Te Kōhanga Shipwreck Bay is well-known for its excellent surf breaks and the namesake shipwreck in the bay is still visible at low tide.
Kaitaia is the main hub for this region, so if you need to stock up on supplies, this is the place to do so. Ninety Mile Beach and Cape Reinga tours also depart from here.

Make the trip to the spiritual northern-most point of the country, Te Rerenga Wairua Cape Reinga, where the oceans collide and the spirits of the departed make the leap to return to their ancestral homeland of Hawaiki. Save your lunch for the return trip home, eating at this sacred site is not permitted.

Visit one of the most important historical sites in the country, where Te Tiriti o Waitangi (The Treaty of Waitangi) was signed in 1840. With two museums, guided tours, cultural performances, an on-site café, and more, you could spend all day at the Waitangi Treaty Grounds. Allow a minimum of 3 hours for the highlights.
Depart for the islands on a boat cruise or ferry, and explore in, on and around the water by kayak, paddleboard, snorkelling, swimming, sailing, basically any which way you like!
Whangārei Heads is home to some of Department of Conservation’s best short and day walks including the epic Mount Manaia hike which serves up breath-taking views over the Whangārei Harbour.
